lead.hed: USS Makin Island pulled into Yokosuka with the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit
lead.insight: A Navy photograph dated Oct. 26 shows the Wasp-class amphibious assault ship USS Makin Island (LHD 8) pulling into Commander, Fleet Activities Yokosuka. The caption calls her the flagship of the Makin Island Amphibious Ready Group, underway with the 13th Marine Expeditionary Unit in the U.S. 7th Fleet area of operations. The photo page does not list a port-call length or a next sailing date.
lead.image_credit: Mass Communication Specialist Seaman Kaitlyn Ratliff · DVIDS 10047721 · Public domain · USS Makin Island (LHD 8) pulls into Commander, Fleet Activities Yokosuka, Oct. 26, 2026.

political.hed: The Pentagon named USS Colorado the first U.S. boat for Australia's submarine rotation
political.insight: Defense News reported Monday that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, with British and Australian counterparts, named the Virginia-class fast-attack submarine USS Colorado (SSN 788) as the first U.S. boat assigned to Submarine Rotational Force-West. The force is expected to be fully operational in 2027 at HMAS Stirling near Perth, with four U.S. boats and one British boat. The Pentagon statement said the rotation is meant to speed Australia's readiness to own and maintain a conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarine.

political.hed: The Army tested temporary battlefield graves at Fort Bragg so remains can still come home
political.insight: An Army release on Phase II of Operation Dragon Covenant says soldiers from the 3rd Corps Sustainment Command, the 20th Engineer Brigade, and unit ministry teams practiced large-scale temporary interment near the St. Mere Eglise Drop Zone. The release says the Army has not done this at scale since the Korean War. Engineers had to dig and refill plots without collapsing mock remains, so later teams could identify and return every soldier. Defense News reported the exercise on Monday.

political.hed: A British committee says the Royal Navy cannot defend the High North from Russia
political.insight: USNI News reported Monday that the House of Commons Defense Committee, in a report titled Defense in the High North, said the Royal Navy lacks the ships and capabilities to defend the High North from Russia. The committee described the fleet as plagued by shipbuilding trouble. The article page did not open for a longer quote; the item follows the USNI summary.

tech.hed: Helsing offered two interceptor missiles aimed at Russia's faster Geran drones
tech.insight: Defense News reported from Cologne that German firm Helsing showed a pair of air-defense missiles, plus software to organize intercepts, priced under $100,000 a shot. Chief executive Gundbert Scherf said the Contra suite is in testing and aimed at market readiness in the second half of 2027. He said newer Geran-4 and Geran-5 drones fly at 400 to 700 kilometers per hour, and that almost half now get through. The jet-powered Inferno is listed at 700 kilometers per hour and a 20-kilometer range.

tech.hed: A new Philippine patrol ship shadowed China's Liaoning carrier group off Mindanao
tech.insight: USNI News reported from Manila that the Philippine Coast Guard's new patrol vessel BRP Sarangani (6177), built in Taiwan, shadowed the Chinese Navy's Liaoning carrier strike group on Friday off Mindanao. The group included the 60,000-ton carrier Liaoning (16) and the guided-missile destroyer Anshan (101). The article page did not open for a longer quote; the item follows the USNI summary.

tech.hed: USNI posted its Monday chart of deployed carriers and amphibious groups
tech.insight: USNI News published its Fleet and Marine Tracker for Oct. 26. The summary says the chart shows approximate positions of deployed carrier strike groups and amphibious ready groups from Navy and public data, and that a split group is plotted at the capital ship. The article page did not open for the plot itself.

culture.hed: Law & Liberty measures 2026 against Magna Carta and the Mayflower Compact
culture.insight: A Monday Law & Liberty essay notes that 2026, the 250th year of the Declaration, sits farther from the Mayflower Compact (406 years) than that compact sat from Magna Carta in 1215 (405 years). The writer treats the Declaration as a summary of both documents: written limits on power, and a people governing themselves. It is an argument about continuity, not a bill or a vote.
